title: Derived global trace adjunction over an affine scheme
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived tensor is computed by K-flat resolutions and derived direct image by K-injective resolutions. A perfect complex is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $f:X\to Y$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces. Let $a:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be a supplied right adjoint of $Rf_*$, with counit $\epsilon:Rf_*a\to\mathrm{id}$. Put $W=a(\mathcal O_Y)$. For $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ write $G(L)=R\Gamma(X,L)\in D(A)$ and $\mathsf H_X(L,W)=R\Gamma(X,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(L,W))\in D(A)$, using global sections [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then the evaluation-and-counit pairing induces a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$, $$\tau_L:\mathsf H_X(L,W)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(G(L),A[0]).$$ Here module derived Hom is internal Hom on the one-object ringed site of $A$. More precisely, with the trace $t:G(W)\cong R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*W)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(\epsilon_{\mathcal O_Y})}A[0]$, the adjunct pairing of $\tau_L$ is $$G(R\mathcal Hom_X(L,W))\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}G(L)\longrightarrow G(R\mathcal Hom_X(L,W)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}L)\xrightarrow{G(\mathrm{ev})}G(W)\xrightarrow{t}A[0].$$ The first map is the canonical cup product. In every integer degree $n$, the canonical identification $H^n\mathsf H_X(L,W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(L,W[n])$ takes $H^n(\tau_L)$ to the ordinary adjunction map, followed by the affine derived-module equivalence. Internal Hom on $X$ need not have quasi-coherent cohomology for this assertion.

proof.text:
Let $G_Y=R\Gamma(Y,-)$. The derived direct-image composition comparison gives $G\cong G_YRf_*$, naturally in the input, including $W$ and its shifts. The affine equivalence gives $G_Y(\mathcal O_Y)\cong A[0]$. Thus $t=G_Y(\epsilon_{\mathcal O_Y})$ under these comparisons is a map $G(W)\to A[0]$. Apply the global cup/Hom comparison to $(L,W)$, and postcompose in module derived Hom with $t$. Define
$$\tau_L=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(G(L),t)\circ\chi_{L,W}.$$
The tensor-Hom transpose formula says its adjunct is $t\circ G(\mathrm{ev})\circ c$, exactly the pairing in the statement. This constructs an actual map in $D(A)$, natural in $L$.

proof.text:
Fix an integer $n$. By the shifted Hom normalization of $\chi$, the degree-$n$ map of $\tau_L$ sends $u:L\to W[n]$ to $t[n]\circ G(u)$. Naturality of the composition comparison identifies this with
$$G_Y\bigl(\epsilon_{\mathcal O_Y}[n]\circ Rf_*u\bigr):G_Y(Rf_*L)\longrightarrow G_Y(\mathcal O_Y)[n],$$
where $Rf_*u$ includes the canonical shift comparison $Rf_*(W[n])\cong(Rf_*W)[n]$. The target Hom identification is the one in the global cup/Hom lemma applied to the one-object ringed site of $A$. Hence this calculation proves precisely the claimed cohomology normalization.

source.place: Tag 0E58 proof, adjunction equality tested on the structure sheaf and its shifts; sites Tags 08JA and 0B6D

proof.text: The morphism $u\mapsto\epsilon_{\mathcal O_Y}[n]\circ Rf_*u$ is the bijection of the supplied adjunction, applied to $L$ and $\mathcal O_Y[n]$; the right-adjoint shift identification $a(\mathcal O_Y[n])\cong a(\mathcal O_Y)[n]$ is the one induced by the adjunction and the shift comparison for $Rf_*$. Both $L$ and $W[n]$ lie in the full quasi-coherent subcategory, so its Hom sets are the ambient derived Hom sets. Both $Rf_*L$ and $\mathcal O_Y[n]$ lie in the analogous subcategory on $Y$: the first because $Rf_*$ of the quasi-compact quasi-separated $f$ sends $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ into $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ (here with $S=Y$), the second because $\mathcal O_Y$ is quasi-coherent. Full faithfulness of the affine equivalence identifies its Hom sets with those of $D(A)$. Step 2 therefore shows that $H^n(\tau_L)$ is bijective for every $n$.

source.place: Tag 0E58 proof, third equality, and Tag 0E59 proof, testing on shifts; spaces-perfect Tag 071Q

proof.text: A morphism in $D(A)$ inducing isomorphisms in every cohomological degree is invertible: represent it by a roof of module complexes $C\xleftarrow{s}B\xrightarrow{h}D$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Since $H^n(s)$ and the cohomology maps of the roof are invertible, every $H^n(h)$ is invertible; thus $h$ also is a quasi-isomorphism, and both arrows become invertible in the localization. Apply this to $\tau_L$. Its naturality was built into step 1. No step required quasi-coherence of $R\mathcal Hom_X(L,W)$.
